summary.en: Use numerical arrays, inspect their shapes and apply indexing, vectorized calculations and broadcasting.
summary.bn: NumPy অ্যারের শেপ দেখো, ইনডেক্স দিয়ে মান নাও আর পুরো অ্যারেতে একসঙ্গে হিসাব করো।

notes: The Python syntax works on 3.10 and later; optional library releases have their own interpreter requirements.

sections.title: Treat a table of marks as one numerical object
Build arrays and inspect their dimensions
Follow axes through indexing and arithmetic
See numerical operations and shared storage
Choose values without losing track of ownership
Check meaning before trusting a result
Separate language syntax from library support
Read the shape as part of the calculation

examples.title: Compare repetition with numerical multiplication
examples.explanationHtml: The list repeats its items. NumPy doubles each number; converting back with tolist gives ordinary Python values.

examples.title: Follow rows and columns through a reduction
examples.explanationHtml: Two rows represent two students, and three columns represent three quizzes. axis=1 reduces each row to one mean.

examples.title: Select passing marks with a mask
examples.explanationHtml: The comparison produces one boolean per mark. Boolean indexing keeps only the entries whose mask is True.

examples.title: Broadcast one adjustment per column
examples.explanationHtml: The length-three bonus aligns with the last dimension. Both student rows receive the same three adjustments.

examples.title: Distinguish a slice view from a copy
examples.explanationHtml: Basic slicing shares storage. Changing the slice changes the original, while changing the explicit copy does not.

practice.title: Apply a capped bonus
practice.statementHtml: Read one line of 0–100 integer marks, possibly blank, followed by an integer bonus from 0–20. Print the adjusted marks separated by spaces, capped at 100; an empty result prints a blank line.
hints: Use np.minimum after addition, then convert the integer elements to text.

practice.title: Calculate two subject averages
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 1–100, then n lines containing two integer marks from 0–100. Print the two column means on one line, each with two decimal places.
hints: Build an n by 2 array and reduce along axis zero.

practice.title: Count a closed interval
practice.statementHtml: Read a possibly blank line of integer scores from 0–100. Read low and high on the next line, where 0 ≤ low ≤ high ≤ 100. Print how many scores lie in the inclusive interval.
hints: Combine parenthesized masks with &, then count their True entries.

practice.title: Center each student row
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 1–50, followed by n lines of exactly three integer marks from 0–100. Subtract each row mean from its entries. Print each centered row with two decimal places; display rounded zero as 0.00.
hints: keepdims=True retains a length-one column for broadcasting; normalize numbers that round to zero.

quiz.prompt: How does NumPy multiplication differ from list repetition for [2, 3]?
quiz.explanation: Array multiplication applies to each entry; list multiplication repeats the sequence.

quiz.prompt: Which shape remains after selecting the second column of a two-by-three array?
quiz.explanation: An integer column index removes that axis.

quiz.prompt: Which original entry changes through the slice window?
quiz.explanation: The slice starts at original index one and shares its data.
quiz.code:
import numpy as np


def main():
    a = np.array([1, 2, 3])
    b = a[1:]
    b[0] = 9
    print(a.tolist())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

quiz.prompt: Which shape broadcasts against shape (4, 3) without adding a new axis?
quiz.explanation: Dimensions align from the right and must be equal or one.

quiz.prompt: Which expression computes one total per row of a matrix?
quiz.explanation: Reducing the column axis leaves a total for each row.

quiz.prompt: What does dtype describe in a numerical ndarray?
options: The representation used for its elements
quiz.explanation: A numerical array stores elements using a common representation.

quiz.prompt: How should two elementwise comparisons be combined in a NumPy mask?
quiz.explanation: Use elementwise operators with parentheses; and requests a single truth value.

quiz.prompt: Why can fixed-width NumPy integers overflow?
options: Their representation has a bounded range
quiz.explanation: Python int can grow, but a selected NumPy integer dtype has fixed limits.

quiz.prompt: Which operation guarantees independent storage for this basic slice?
quiz.explanation: copy creates a separate data buffer.

quiz.prompt: Why print a computed array mean using an explicit decimal format?
quiz.explanation: Formatting controls text; it does not remove floating-point approximation.

quiz.prompt: What is required before reshape(2, 3) can reshape a one-dimensional array?

keyPoints.en: Numerical arrays apply arithmetic to entries rather than repeating lists.
keyPoints.bn: লিস্টে গুণ করলে আইটেমগুলো আবার আসে, কিন্তু NumPy অ্যারেতে প্রতিটা মানে গুণ হয়।

keyPoints.en: Shape describes axis lengths, while ndim counts axes.
keyPoints.bn: শেপ বলে প্রতিটা অ্যাক্সিসে কয়টা মান আছে, আর ndim বলে অ্যাক্সিস কয়টা।

keyPoints.en: Broadcasting compares dimensions from the right.
keyPoints.bn: ব্রডকাস্টিংয়ের সময় ডান দিক থেকে ডাইমেনশন মিলিয়ে দেখো।

keyPoints.en: Basic slices can share storage; copy separates it.
keyPoints.bn: সাধারণ স্লাইসের মান বদলালে আসল অ্যারেও বদলাতে পারে, তাই আলাদা রাখতে copy করো।

keyPoints.en: Boolean masks select entries and need elementwise logical operators.
keyPoints.bn: বুলিয়ান মাস্ক দিয়ে দরকারি মান বাছাই করো, আর শর্ত জুড়তে & ব্যবহার করো।

keyPoints.en: Decimal formatting stabilizes displayed precision without changing numeric accuracy.
keyPoints.bn: কয় ঘর দশমিক দেখাবে তা ফরম্যাটে ঠিক করো, তবে এতে হিসাবের নির্ভুলতা বাড়ে না।

examQuestions.question: Explain list multiplication and NumPy multiplication using [10, 20] and a multiplier of 2.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The list becomes [10, 20, 10, 20]. The numerical array contains [20, 40]. List multiplication repeats references; NumPy multiplication computes a value for each entry.

examQuestions.question: Trace shape (2, 3) plus shapes (3,), (2, 1) and (2,).
examQuestions.answerHtml: (3,) aligns with the last axis and adds one value per column. (2, 1) stretches its final length-one axis and adds one value per row. (2,) conflicts with the final length three, so addition raises ValueError.

examQuestions.question: Explain why row centering needs keepdims=True.
examQuestions.answerHtml: For an n by 3 array, mean(axis=1) has shape (n,). Keeping dimensions gives shape (n, 1), which broadcasts along columns. Without that retained axis, subtraction can fail or, when n is three, align the wrong way silently.
